npmjs.ci-publish: by design: the page (CI) says a provider should not build a CI publish path on a bypass-2FA token, and trusted publishing is held by npm, not by a provider, so the reference provider answers no interactive-false publish; this is the provider's choice, not a statement that npmjs.com has no such request
npmjs.unsupported: by design: the reference provider maps every operation of the protocol to an endpoint it documents for npmjs.com, so it never answers `operation-not-supported`; a provider that declines an operation would
npmjs.401-erase: by design: the reference provider hands out the stored token itself, so after a rejection it holds no other credential to release and the retry can only be `other` (Phase 2, retry rules); another provider that mints or refreshes a credential would show this exchange, and the 401-dead row shows the stored-token one

gitlab.stage: unknown: GitLab's npm registry page documents no staging or approval step (an absence in the docs, not a documented refusal); a publish is live at once (the page, Staging)

corporate-sso.stage: n/a: the gateway has no staging, no tokens, no teams and no trust endpoints (the page, Publish)

github-packages.stage: unknown: the GitHub Packages npm page never mentions staging and the staged-publishing documents found describe npmjs.com only (an absence in the docs, rechecked 2026-10-20, not verified either way)
github-packages.401-erase: by design: the reference provider hands out the stored token itself, so after a rejection it holds no other credential to release and the retry can only be `other` (Phase 2, retry rules); another provider that mints or refreshes a credential would show this exchange, and the 401-dead row shows the stored-token one

google-artifact-registry.stage: unknown: the pages read for the example describe no staging model (an absence in the pages, not a documented refusal)
google-artifact-registry.not-found: by design: the docs read do not say whether the registry hides a repository from an identity that cannot see it; the reference provider's `not-found` would mean nothing stored, which it does not answer, and hello `registries` stops npm asking for unconfigured registries (the page, Rejection)

jfrog-artifactory.stage: unknown: no Artifactory page read describes staged publishing for npm, and the page itself marks the list of unsupported operations unverified, from memory (an absence, not a documented refusal); stage-unsupported.jsonl shows the reference provider's answer

azure-artifacts.stage: unknown: no Azure Artifacts page read describes staged publishing (an absence in the docs, not proof the endpoints do not exist)

aws-codeartifact.stage: unknown: the CodeArtifact npm pages list no `/-/stage` endpoints; the page reads that as an inference from the absence in AWS's list, not an AWS statement, and the provider answers the stage operations with `operation-not-supported`

verdaccio.401-erase: by design: the reference provider hands out the stored token itself, so after a rejection it holds no other credential to release and the retry can only be `other` (Phase 2, retry rules); another provider that mints or refreshes a credential would show this exchange, and the 401-dead row shows the stored-token one
